content.text:
I submitted **index 174 (Cr 0.15, Fe 0.54, V 0.31)** as the best composition. At 3.94 µA it had the highest photocurrent of the three merit measurements I was allowed.

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 37 | 0.19 / 0.20 / 0.61 (V-rich) | 0.92 µA |
| 14 | 0.16 / 0.43 / 0.42 (Fe:V ≈ 1:1) | 1.75 µA |
| 174 | 0.15 / 0.54 / 0.31 (Fe-rich) | 3.94 µA |

- **Trend:** photocurrent rose with Fe content across the three points, so compositions with even more Fe (around 0.6–0.7) might do better. With no measurements left I couldn't test that, and three points is too few to be sure the best composition in the library isn't somewhere else entirely.
- **Model checks:** before each measurement the rules required a band-gap prediction, which gave 2.1–2.8 eV depending on method. I couldn't open the phase list because the output was too large, so I ran those predictions on `mp-504509`, a phase ID I guessed without knowing what it is. The results only show that some vanadate-type phase would absorb the 3.2 eV light. They didn't guide which composition to pick.
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I don't know which crystal phases are in the samples.
